description: WANDa network GIS. One GeoPackage, one layer per kind (layer name = kind name), EPSG:27700, coordinates in metres. Layers are aligned to the PLDR project tables (app_table / app). The converter changes only layer names, field names and the delivery's own codes; values (coordinates, diameters, lengths, dates, refs) are as delivered. App behaviour comes from ONE rule per code attribute (rules), never from per-client tables. ONE IMPORT, ALL APPS (v1.2): every clean-water layer and field of a delivery comes in - assets of every status and function (abandoned / proposed kept with status, raw / non-potable and service pipes with pipe_function, customer meters with meter_function, other point assets in `assets`) and every source field with no WI field in the row's `extra` bag; the apps take what they need by the rules. Waste-water layers stay out. v1.3: where the delivery left a node ref, pipe ref or area ref blank the import fills it once and records the origin in the *_source field (value_source); the apps never re-derive.

container.polygons: MultiPolygon layers accept Polygon rows. Every polygon in a filed set is valid (OGC): the converter repairs an invalid one as delivered (make_valid, polygon parts kept) and records each repair in wanda_delivery.json (geometry_repaired); the validator refuses an invalid polygon (NW-INVALID). 1.2.1, 16/10/2026
container.row_order: the converter keeps the source row order within each layer (readers that keep the first of duplicate refs depend on it)
container.lines: pipes is a LineString layer: the converter merges a multi-part line whose parts join into one LineString; a multi-part line whose parts do not join is kept as MultiLineString in the same layer with pipes.multipart = '1' (the only multi geometry a line layer may hold)
container.scope: clean water only: every clean-water layer of a delivery is mapped to a WI layer or declared in the mapping's excluded list (the converter reports any delivered layer that is neither); waste-water layers (sewers, drainage areas, waste-water assets) are excluded
container.extra: every layer ends with `confirm` and `extra` (set by the converter, never mapped): `extra` = the source fields with no WI field, as a JSON object keyed by the delivered column name (blank = none); `confirm` = the WI fields of the row whose classification needs confirming (';' list)

types.ref: text exactly as delivered (a float id 12345.0 is written 12345; leading zeros kept); never changed
types.text: free text as delivered (phone numbers / e-mail addresses inside free text are removed)
types.code: a code from the field's code list
types.datetime: ISO 8601 yyyy-mm-dd, or yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss when a time is known
types.json: a JSON object as text (UTF-8), keys = delivered column names, values as delivered (text, number, true / false; dates as ISO text); blank = no keys. Free text inside loses phone numbers / e-mail addresses as any text field

ref_rules: Every *_ref field is text exactly as delivered: trimmed, case kept, leading zeros kept, a float id 12345.0 written 12345.

ref_to names the layer.field a ref points at (a list = any of them; a node ref may name a junction, a pipe end or a point asset that is its own network node, e.g. a valve); ref_check must_exist = an error when the target layer is delivered and the value is missing from it; should_exist = counted and reported (e.g. a node ref to a site / pump junction).

unique lists each layer's key (never blank, except the optional key parts of meter_loggers (channel) and prv_settings (valid_from), which are compared as blank); unique_check warn = duplicates reported, the reader keeps the first (hydrants, meters); a layer with no unique list (dma_areas) may repeat its ref.
Area refs on assets (dma_ref, wqz_ref ...) are the delivery's own; the import fills blank area refs once (dma_ref_source); the apps may also assign by polygon (dma_areas).
A list field holds refs separated by ';' with no spaces.

Node refs: where the delivery left a pipe end or point asset without a usable node ref the import fills it once from the geometry (ends and points within 1 cm share a ref; *_node_source says gis / derived_coincident / derived_own). A derived ref has the form c:<x>_<y> (metres, 3 decimal places, the cluster's lowest end point). No node rows are added; the apps never re-derive.

Meter role (no field, no guessing): for DMA X, a network meter with dma_ref = X is an inlet and one with dma_from_ref = X an export; where dma_from_ref is not delivered the export role is unknown (engineer to say).

Logger locations: a meter's logger links live in meter_loggers; every other logger / monitoring location (critical points, PRV and pump tappings, DMA inlet tappings ...) is a row of monitoring_points.

rules.rule: Every asset is loaded, whatever its status (abandoned / proposed / mothballed kept); only in_network assets build the network the apps analyse (traces, isolation, property links). Blank status counts as unknown (in_network).

A property snaps only to a serves_customers pipe; a delivered properties.pipe_ref is kept as given. pipe_function unknown: serves_customers false and confirm (James 13/10 'probably not, but confirm'). serves_customers null (trunk) = the module decides; the code list does not fix it and client property links are kept as delivered.

Only potable_network pipes enter the potable network: raw / non-potable mains and customer-side supply / other pipes are kept, not analysed. Communication pipes stay potable_network as in v1.1 (James to decide one PLDR pipe set for every client).
An isolates valve stops an isolation trace (gis_valves.is_gate_valve = 1).
A shut valve is a boundary in the network as delivered (closed); unknown and throttled count as open.

Every meter is loaded (customer meters too); only network meters are loaded into gis_meters: district, bulk, reservoir, reservoir_inlet, reservoir_outlet, trunk, supply, source, pump. process, customer, commercial and other are not network meters.
Only is_dma areas become DMA polygons in the apps; other districts are kept, not used as DMAs.
Discolouration risk band of the material (unknown = 3).
Hydrant tier for tankering / injection / overland supply (1 = first choice, 2 = second, 0 = not used).
diameter x factor = mm (per row by diameter_units); coordinates are metres BNG.
A code whose confirm attribute is true is an uncertain class: the converter lists the field in the row's confirm; the apps apply the code's own attributes until staff confirm it.

pipes.description: Water pipes of every function and status: mains (distribution / trunk), raw and non-potable mains, service (communication / supply) pipes, abandoned / proposed pipes - status and pipe_function say which the apps analyse (rules R1-R3). from / to node refs are as delivered: their order may follow digitising or flow (the mapping's app_options.pipe_node_order says which); the apps take topology from the node refs, not from the vertex order. v1.3: blank node refs are filled by the import (derived refs c:<x>_<y>, see ref_rules); the apps take topology from the refs as filed.

One row per meter, system, logger reference and channel; logger reading data is a separate (later) telemetry set. Rows with a blank logger_ref are skipped and counted (skip_blank). monitoring_points.description: Pressure / flow monitoring locations that are not meters: critical points, low level points, DG2 points, PRV inlet / outlet and pump suction / delivery tappings, DMA inlet tappings. One row per logger / monitoring location. A location may point at the asset it sits on (asset_layer + asset_ref) or stand on its own (node_ref, geometry). Meter logger links stay in meter_loggers. Apps may show these sites; PLDR does not use them for flushing or scores.

row_flags: extra: the mapping names the source columns for the bag (extra: [columns]) or takes every delivered column not mapped into a WI field (extra: "*rest"). Never in the bag: personal columns (people's names, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, user / editor ids), sensitive-customer columns (priority services, special needs, medical, vulnerable - see properties.sensitive_customer) and geometry-derived system columns (shape length / area); the converter records the columns it left out. The strict loader refuses a mapping that names a personal or sensitive column anywhere.

confirm: a field is listed when its class is uncertain - the code's `confirm` attribute is true (e.g. pipe_function unknown: serves_customers false, 'probably not, but confirm'), the delivered value had no mapping (the codes fallback, counted) or the mapping lists the delivered value in codes.confirm. The row keeps its own ref, so staff confirm it against the client key outside AI (pick / key tool) or a new WI value is added the normal way.

restricted: a field marked restricted (properties.sensitive_customer, properties.organisation) is a placeholder for data that needs a special sign-in or is never held; no mapping may fill it and the converter never populates it. Fields marked set_by converter (*_source, dma_boundary_refs, meter_function_delivered, source, confirm, extra) are written by the import and never mapped.
Code-list labels are the reporting lookups: every code list's `label` is the display / report name of its codes (WI names), the same for every client.
